title: Making Space for Jacob’s Big Dreams, Rooted in Family Support
summary: Learn more about Jacob, a recent high school graduate with achondroplasia whose dreams stretch from UC Merced to NASA.
body_markdown:
## Family at the Heart


Jacob credits his parents, teachers, mentors and friends for helping open doors to opportunity. His grandmother, Annette, has also been in his corner at every turn.


“I hope people notice Jacob’s smile, intelligence, and confidence before they notice his height,” Annette says. A nurse practitioner by training, she has watched Jacob tackle challenges with quiet courage. “He’s thoughtful, funny, and genuinely curious. I want people to see the remarkable young man he is before the condition he was born with.”


For Annette, everyday moments – watching Jacob prepare for class, hearing his excitement about engineering – are reminders of his drive. This year has carried its share of joy and sorrow: celebrating Jacob’s high school graduation while grieving the death of her husband, Ken. Still, cheering Jacob on as he steps into this new chapter has helped Annette hold onto hope, and find a new sense of purpose.


That renewed aim inspired her to write[Jacob’s Big Dream](https://store.bookbaby.com/book/jacobs-big-dream2?srsltid=AfmBOorKVR-haLAzLGzA-W29NOaPdRjM5tISdV08uK3j-G-o1Nm86vjL) , a children’s book rooted in his story. Jacob’s Big Dream is a heartfelt story inspired by Annette’s experience watching her grandson learn that courage, determination and self-belief can help people overcome life’s biggest challenges.


“I wanted to remind every child that their biggest dream deserves to be pursued, and every adult has the opportunity to help make space for it,” she says. “Dreams don’t grow because life is easy. They grow because someone believes in you until you believe in yourself.”


Jacob notes he was initially hesitant to be featured in the book, but came around to the power of sharing his story with the world.


“After reading the book, I realized my experience could help others navigate their own challenges, and that helped me see how important it was to be part of this endeavor,” he says.


Jacob’s family influence also carried into Junior Reserve Officers’ Training Corps (JROTC), a high school program sponsored by the U.S. Armed Forces that teaches citizenship, leadership and personal responsibility. Inspired by his great-grandfather, a military veteran and one of his biggest influences, Jacob found in JROTC a way to experience military values even though his diagnosis prevented him from enlisting. The program also continued a family tradition, with his father and siblings having participated before him, and gave Jacob a strong sense of belonging.


“It was definitely a positive experience,” Jacob says. “It was like having a second family at school.”
